findings.source_passage: for there is no folly of the beasts of the earth which is not infinitely outdone by the madness of men.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Stripped to our shirts and drawers'
findings.why_it_matters: This is one of the chapter's most quotable, critically-cited sentences—a gnomic epigram on collective human panic. The draft renders it as 'there is no folly of beasts not outdone by the madness of men,' dropping 'infinitely' and 'of the earth,' gutting the rhetorical weight and cadence of the original.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore verbatim: 'for there is no folly of the beasts of the earth which is not infinitely outdone by the madness of men.'

findings.source_passage: as human infants while suckling will calmly and fixedly gaze away from the breast, as if leading two different lives at the time; and while yet drawing mortal nourishment, be still spiritually feasting upon some unearthly reminiscence
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'But far beneath this wondrous world'
findings.why_it_matters: This extended simile—one of the chapter's most philosophically loaded passages, linking whale calves to human infants 'leading two different lives'—is entirely cut. It is interpretively central to readings of the chapter's mystical-maternal theme and is prosodically unique.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the simile: 'as human infants while suckling will calmly and fixedly gaze away from the breast, as if leading two different lives at the time; and while yet drawing mortal nourishment, be still spiritually feasting upon some unearthly reminiscence—even so did the young of these whales seem looking up towards us, but not at us.'

findings.source_passage: the unborn whale lies bent like a Tartar's bow
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'But far beneath this wondrous world'
findings.why_it_matters: The Tartar's bow image is a memorably distinctive and oft-cited figure—one of Melville's most concrete, exotic comparisons in the chapter. Its absence strips a key signature image from the description of the infant whale.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore: 'where, tail to head, and all ready for the final spring, the unborn whale lies bent like a Tartar's bow.'

findings.source_passage: So Ahab. Mark this, too, in the whaler. While other hulls are loaded down with alien stuff… She is ballasted with utilities; not altogether with unusable pig-lead and kentledge.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'But how now? in this zoned quest'
findings.why_it_matters: The 'So Ahab' epigram and the 'ballasted with utilities' passage are distinctive voice-establishing rhetoric, closely parallel to the narrator's ironic-digressive mode; both are excised, leaving only the ark punchline without the buildup.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at minimum: 'So Ahab. Mark this, too, in the whaler. While other hulls are loaded down with alien stuff…She is ballasted with utilities; not altogether with unusable pig-lead and kentledge.'

findings.source_passage: And who could tell whether, in that congregated caravan, Moby Dick himself might not temporarily be swimming, like the worshipped white-elephant in the coronation procession of the Siamese!
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Crowding all sail the Pequod pressed after them'
findings.why_it_matters: This is both an interpretive keystone—Moby Dick may be among the herd—and a memorably distinctive simile (the Siamese white elephant). Its absence removes a moment of suspense and thematic resonance central to the chapter.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore: 'And who could tell whether, in that congregated caravan, Moby Dick himself might not temporarily be swimming, like the worshipped white-elephant in the coronation procession of the Siamese!'

findings.source_passage: The milk is very sweet and rich; it has been tasted by man; it might do well with strawberries. When overflowing with mutual esteem, the whales salute more hominum.
findings.source_locator: footnote to 'We saw young Leviathan amours in the deep.'
findings.why_it_matters: The footnote's wry, irreverent close—particularly 'it might do well with strawberries' and 'salute more hominum'—is a well-known Melvillean comic aside, part of the chapter's tonal signature. Its complete absence erases a register-defining moment.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the footnote (even condensed) with at minimum: 'The milk is very sweet and rich; it has been tasted by man; it might do well with strawberries. When overflowing with mutual esteem, the whales salute more hominum.'

findings.source_passage: not only that, but a herd of remorseless wild pirates and inhuman atheistical devils were infernally cheering him on with their curses
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'As if too long lurking behind the headlands'
findings.why_it_matters: The draft renders this as 'infernally cheered on with curses'—losing 'remorseless wild pirates and inhuman atheistical devils,' which is tonally and rhetorically distinctive; 'atheistical devils' in particular is a characteristic Melville register-marker.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore: 'remorseless wild pirates and inhuman atheistical devils were infernally cheering him on with their curses.'

summary: The draft has one clearly verbatim high-severity signature loss ('infinitely outdone'), one major interpretive-weight passage absent (infant-whale suckling simile with 'two different lives'), one signature image absent ('bent like a Tartar's bow'), and multiple medium-severity losses including Moby Dick/white-elephant, 'So Ahab'/'ballasted with utilities,' the comic footnote, and the 'atheistical devils' phrasing, collectively requiring regeneration.
